record.original_question: Does every subgroup of a solvable group have bounded packing, in the sense that for every radius r > 0 there is a uniform bound N after which any N distinct left cosets must contain a pair whose distance is at least r in a proper left-invariant metric on the group?

evidence.quote: We say that H has bounded packing in G, if given any r > 0 we can find a number N, which may depend on G, H, and r, such that any collection of N distinct left cosets of H in G {g1H, ..., gN H} contains a pair giH, gjH which is separated by distance at least r, or d(giH, gjH) >= r.
In light of Theorem 3.2.7 one can ask the question whether every subgroup of a solvable group has bounded packing. While an affirmative answer to this question is unlikely...

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finitely generated group equipped with a proper left-invariant metric $d$ (for example, a word metric with respect to a finite generating set). For a subgroup $H \le G$, define the distance between two left cosets $g_1 H$ and $g_2 H$ by
$$d(g_1 H, g_2 H) \;=\; \inf\{\, d(g_1 h_1, g_2 h_2) : h_1, h_2 \in H \,\}.$$
Say that $H$ has bounded packing in $G$ if for every $r > 0$ there exists an integer $N = N(G, H, r)$ such that any collection of $N$ distinct left cosets $g_1 H, \dots, g_N H$ contains at least one pair $g_i H, g_j H$ (with $i \ne j$) satisfying $d(g_i H, g_j H) \ge r$.

Question: Does every subgroup $H$ of every (finitely generated) solvable group $G$ have bounded packing in $G$?
artifact.category_tag: Geometric group theory: bounded packing in solvable groups
artifact.status_search_result: The question (in this full generality, for all subgroups of all solvable groups) has a negative answer. A finitely generated solvable group of derived length 3 has been constructed that contains a finitely generated subgroup failing bounded packing, refuting the broad version of the Hruska–Wise question. Positive results are known in restricted classes (e.g., subgroups of virtually nilpotent or nilpotent-by-polycyclic groups have bounded packing); the conjecture restricted to virtually polycyclic groups remains of interest.

status_evidence.title: Packing subgroups in solvable groups
status_evidence.snippet: Packing subgroups in solvable groups — constructs a finitely generated solvable group of derived length 3 having a finitely generated subgroup without the bounded packing property.
status_evidence.claim: There exists a finitely generated solvable group of derived length 3 with a finitely generated subgroup failing bounded packing, giving a negative answer to the general question.

status_evidence.title: Packing subgroups in relatively hyperbolic groups (Hruska–Wise)
status_evidence.snippet: Defines bounded packing and asks/conjectures about subgroups of solvable / virtually polycyclic groups; proves bounded packing in various settings.
status_evidence.claim: Hruska–Wise introduced bounded packing and posed the question for solvable groups; positive results are known in restricted subclasses.
